spreadsheet.title: How to Use a LitBuy Spreadsheet: Find Products and Buy Step by Step
spreadsheet.description: Learn how to search a LitBuy spreadsheet, open the source listing, choose a variant, review warehouse QC and plan shipping before paying.
sections: What a LitBuy spreadsheet does

A LitBuy spreadsheet is a product research list. It helps you compare names, categories, reference prices, images and links before using a shopping agent. The spreadsheet is not an order confirmation, stock guarantee or proof of product authenticity. LitBuyVIP is an independent research site; our product links open the corresponding kakobuymake.com catalog page. That catalog page and the seller listing are separate from your LitBuy account.
The practical sequence is research → verify listing → place an eligible order in the agent account → inspect warehouse evidence → arrange shipping. Keeping these stages separate prevents a cheap reference price from being mistaken for a delivered price.
1. Search by category, name or catalog ID

Use the ten category shortcuts to browse shoes, T-shirts, fashion clothing, hoodies, trousers, belts, hats, bags, accessories and electronics. The homepage search covers the 12 references displayed here. For a larger selection, open the complete main catalog.
A search for 2844, for example, finds the Nike Hyperdunk reference in this local list. This number is a main-catalog record ID, not a Weidian seller item ID. You can also paste a kakobuymake.com product link containing aid=2844. A seller URL containing another kind of ID must be checked on its own source platform; do not assume that the numbers are interchangeable.
2. Open the product and verify the live listing

Open the exact product page rather than the catalog homepage. Check that the product name, photos and selected variation agree. Then review the underlying marketplace listing: seller, price, stock, size, color, quantity and domestic delivery. Prices in this spreadsheet are references and exclude international shipping.
If a link is unavailable, search the main catalog by product name or category. Do not substitute a visually similar listing without comparing the variation and seller. Save the original URL and the listing details you used for your decision.
3. Choose the variant before ordering

A listing with many styles does not describe one interchangeable product. A displayed starting price can apply only to the cheapest variant. Select the exact SKU and recheck the resulting price. For shoes, use the seller’s size chart and request an appropriate measurement if needed. For hoodies and trousers, compare garment measurements with an item you already own.
Before paying, record the product URL, selected SKU, size, color, quantity, quoted product price, domestic delivery and any service fee. Check whether the account accepts the item and whether an international route supports its attributes. A successful domestic order does not establish international shipping eligibility.
4. Review warehouse QC and resolve problems

When the item is recorded at the warehouse, compare QC photos with your saved order details. Check quantity, color, labels, visible condition and the specific dimensions that matter for fit. If a question remains, request a focused photo or measurement and check its fee before confirming.
Keep an incorrect or damaged item out of the international parcel while you check return eligibility. Warehouse storage and seller return deadlines are different. Save arrival dates and act on seller issues promptly. Photographs help with visible checks; they cannot establish authenticity or reveal every hidden defect.
5. Calculate the delivered cost

Add product cost, domestic delivery, applicable account or payment fees, international freight, selected packing services and destination charges that apply. Compare routes using the packed actual weight and dimensions. A light shoe box may be billed by volume. Rehearsal packing can be useful when dimensions are uncertain; check the account’s fee and timing.
For a worked budget, imagine two products costing 120 CNY and 180 CNY, with 15 CNY combined domestic delivery. Your known purchase subtotal is 315 CNY. International freight, optional services and destination charges remain separate unknowns until verified. This example is arithmetic, not a live LitBuy quotation.
Example: research a hoodie without guessing its size

Open the Polo Bear hoodie reference (catalog ID 2813), inspect the current source page and find the selected variant’s chart. Measure a hoodie that fits you: chest laid flat, body length and sleeve length. Compare using the same units and measuring method. Save the requested variant, then check the warehouse measurement for that variant rather than relying on the size label alone.
The purchase can proceed only when the live price, seller terms, fit and shipping eligibility are acceptable. If the chart or QC measurement is missing, request that evidence. The product photo on this site is a catalog illustration, not a new measurement or a warehouse QC sample.
Questions before you buy

Is the spreadsheet itself the official LitBuy service? No. Use the official account for purchase, payment and parcel instructions. Does the reference price include shipping? No; calculate the separate cost components. Can a catalog ID be pasted into every agent? No; verify the actual marketplace product URL.
Keep a short record for each purchase: source URL, chosen SKU, listing price, QC decision, seller deadline, accepted route and final parcel cost. That record makes buying decisions easier to review and problems easier to explain to support.

sizing.title: LitBuy Size Guide: Measure Shoes, Hoodies and Pants Before Buying
sizing.description: Choose LitBuy product sizes using seller charts, garment measurements and focused QC requests. Worked examples for shoes, hoodies and pants.
sections: Start with measurements, not a universal size conversion

There is no single LitBuy size chart that covers every seller and product. A label such as M, EU 42 or W32 is a reference; it does not establish how a specific variant fits. Use the selected listing’s chart and compare like-for-like measurements. This guide describes a measurement workflow, not a promise that any catalog item runs true to size.
You need three pieces of evidence: the seller’s chart for the chosen SKU, measurements from something that fits you, and warehouse measurements when uncertainty matters. Save them together before the seller’s return window ends.
Shoes: separate foot length from insole length

Measure each foot standing on a flat surface, ideally wearing the socks you plan to use. Mark heel and longest toe, measure in centimeters, and use the longer foot. Check whether the seller’s chart is based on foot length, inner length or a size label; those are different quantities.
For illustration, a 26.0 cm foot does not mean you should automatically choose a 26.0 cm insole. Toe space, shoe shape and the chart’s measuring convention matter. Do not apply a fixed universal allowance. If fit is uncertain, ask for the selected size’s insole measurement or the seller’s recommendation and compare with a similar shoe you own. Some shoes have non-removable insoles, so ask whether the measurement is feasible before paying for it.
Hoodies: compare flat width, length and sleeve method

Lay a well-fitting hoodie flat without stretching it. Measure chest width from armpit to armpit, body length from the specified shoulder point, shoulder width where the garment has a defined seam, and sleeve length using the same start point as the seller. A raglan sleeve and a shoulder-seam sleeve need different comparisons.
Suppose your hoodie is 58 cm wide and 70 cm long, while a seller chart gives 56 cm and 68 cm for one size. The candidate is 2 cm narrower when laid flat and 2 cm shorter. Doubling the flat chest widths gives an illustrative 116 cm versus 112 cm circumference; this is not the same as body chest circumference. The chart’s tolerance and construction still affect fit.
Pants: check waist method, rise and inseam

Measure trousers laid flat: waistband width, front rise, thigh width at a defined distance below the crotch, inseam and leg opening. If the waistband stretches, ask whether the chart lists relaxed or stretched width. Check whether a seller’s waist value is full circumference or flat width.
A 40 cm flat waistband corresponds roughly to an 80 cm circumference if measured without stretching. It should not be compared directly with a chart value of 40 cm circumference. For a practical comparison, pants with a 74 cm inseam will be 3 cm shorter along the inner leg than a reference pair measured at 77 cm. The rise and intended fit may change where the hem sits.
Write a focused warehouse measurement request

Specify the item and variant, the required measurement, the unit, the start and end points, and whether the garment should lie flat without stretching. A useful request is: “For this hoodie SKU, please photograph chest width armpit to armpit and body length using a visible centimeter tape.” A vague request to “check size” is harder to act on.
Check the fee and feasibility before requesting extra photos. Keep the full photo so both tape endpoints are visible. Camera perspective and a folded garment can distort the result. If the measurement looks inconsistent, ask for clarification rather than treating a blurred number as proof.
Use catalog examples as references, not QC evidence

The main catalog contains a shoe reference at ID 2844 and a hoodie reference at ID 2813. Open their current product pages for available listing information and QC references. The catalog images reproduced on this site do not show a newly verified tape measurement. We do not attach invented warehouse measurements to them.
For trousers, start from the pants category and choose a live listing with a readable chart. There is no specific trousers measurement sample verified in this site’s 12-product snapshot. The numerical examples above are hypothetical comparisons intended to explain the method.
Decide before international shipping

Compare the evidence with your acceptable fit range. If the variant is wrong or the dimensions are clearly unsuitable, check seller return or exchange eligibility promptly. Do not ship an uncertain garment internationally hoping that its label will solve the fit issue.
A small difference may be acceptable for a loose hoodie and unacceptable for fitted trousers. Choose according to your reference garment and intended use. Record your decision with the measurement photo, seller chart and selected SKU so you can reuse the comparison next time.
Size questions answered

Does EU 42 always mean the same length? No; check the product chart and its measuring basis. Is flat chest width the same as chest circumference? No; flat width is roughly half the garment circumference when measured consistently. Can QC photos guarantee fit? No; they provide evidence to compare, not a fit guarantee.
A useful size record includes units, measurement method, chosen variant, chart tolerance, reference-item dimensions and warehouse result. That is more reliable than a universal recommendation to size up or size down.

us-shipping.title: LitBuy Shipping to the USA: Compare Cost, Weight and Delivery Routes
us-shipping.description: Plan LitBuy shipping to the USA with packed weight, parcel dimensions, postcode eligibility and route terms. Use worked examples to compare complete quotes.
sections: A useful US shipping quote needs parcel details

There is no reliable universal price for “a LitBuy haul to the USA.” Quotes depend on destination, accepted product attributes, packed weight, dimensions, the selected route and the date of the quotation. This guide provides a comparison method and hypothetical weight examples. It does not publish a live rate card or promise a delivery time.
Start with a US destination and ZIP code, item list, packed actual weight and outer dimensions. Check that the address is accepted by the route, including any restrictions concerning remote areas, PO boxes or special destinations. A route shown for another buyer’s parcel may be unavailable for yours.
Actual weight and volumetric weight can produce different bills

Actual weight is the mass of the final packed parcel. Volumetric weight is calculated from the outer dimensions using the route’s divisor. Many routes compare the two, but you must verify the selected route’s billing rule and rounding. The inbound item weights are not a substitute for the final packed data.
Consider a hypothetical parcel weighing 4.0 kg and measuring 40 × 30 × 25 cm. Its volume is 30,000 cm³. With an illustrative divisor of 6,000, volumetric weight is 5.0 kg; with 5,000, it is 6.0 kg. These divisors are examples, not verified LitBuy US route settings. Use the calculator below with the divisor actually shown in your account.
Compare complete quotes for the same parcel

Record each available route’s name, quote date, billing rule, minimum or increment, parcel limits, accepted item attributes, base freight, surcharges, optional services, valid discount and final payable amount. Compare the same destination and packed data across routes. Include packing or reinforcement only when it is selected and actually charged.
If one quote includes a discount and another does not, compare the resulting payable totals rather than the headline percentages. A coupon can have a cap, expiry, minimum spend and route or account restrictions. Destination charges and any tax treatment require a separate check of current official route terms and applicable destination requirements; do not assume that a label settles every charge.
Read delivery estimates as stages

Separate seller dispatch, domestic delivery, warehouse receiving, QC, packing, handoff, international transit and final-mile delivery. A route’s transit estimate may start after carrier acceptance rather than when you paid for the product. Check the wording and whether it uses calendar or working days.
Avoid planning around a single community delivery report. Processing delays, flights, weather and other handling can change a parcel’s progress. For a deadline-sensitive purchase, compare the current quoted range with your available time and leave a margin. No fixed arrival date is verified in this guide.
Packaging example: lower volume without damaging the goods

Suppose a 4.0 kg parcel is repacked from 40 × 30 × 25 cm to 40 × 30 × 20 cm. With an illustrative divisor of 6,000, the dimensional result falls from 5.0 kg to 4.0 kg. If that route bills the higher of actual and dimensional weight, it could change the billed tier before rounding. The actual saving still depends on the route’s rates and repacking fee.
Remove disposable cartons only when appropriate. Preserve support for fragile or structured items and separate scratch-prone surfaces. A protected bag or electronic item may need packaging that ordinary clothing does not. Compare the complete cost and protection trade-off before approving a change.
Restricted items and mixed parcels

Check the route’s accepted attributes before placing the order and again after packing. Batteries, liquids, powders and other special categories may require a different route or may not be eligible. Do not infer acceptance from a seller’s willingness to ship domestically. A mixed parcel can inherit the limitations of its most restrictive item.
When comparing one box with two boxes, include repeated minimum freight, separate handling, packaging and tracking. Splitting is not automatically cheaper, but it can help when item attributes or size limits prevent an otherwise suitable route. Use live accepted-route quotes for both configurations.
Before paying and after dispatch

Save the route terms and complete checkout breakdown. Confirm the final packed weight, outer dimensions, destination, included items, declared information required by the platform and the actual discount. If you use rehearsal packing, check the service charge, cancellation terms and account workflow before proceeding.
After handoff, save both the agent parcel number and the carrier tracking number. They can be different. Use the carrier identified in the parcel record for delivery scans and ask support with the parcel ID when the expected processing range is exceeded.
US shipping questions

How much does a 5 kg LitBuy parcel to the USA cost? A current accepted-route quote is required; weight alone is insufficient. Is the fastest advertised route always available? No; destination, item and parcel limits matter. Does rehearsal guarantee lower freight? No; it supplies better parcel data.
A reusable quote sheet should contain ZIP code, items, actual weight, dimensions, divisor, rounded billing weight, route, complete payable cost, estimated range and quote date. That lets you compare your own next parcel without treating someone else’s example as a rate card.

tracking.title: LitBuy Order Status and Tracking: From Purchase to Delivery
tracking.description: Understand LitBuy order, warehouse, packing and parcel tracking stages. Learn which number to check and what evidence to send when progress stalls.
sections: An order number and a tracking number serve different stages

A shopping-agent order usually describes the product purchase. Domestic tracking describes seller-to-warehouse delivery. A warehouse record confirms what was received. An international parcel number groups selected stored items, and the carrier tracking number follows the shipped box. These identifiers are related but should not be treated as interchangeable.
Exact status wording varies with the account interface and route. The stage descriptions below are a reading guide, not a verified list of LitBuy interface labels. Match the meaning and accompanying timestamps in your own record.
Purchase submitted and seller dispatch

Check the selected SKU, payment record and any agent message first. An order submitted for purchase may still need review, seller stock confirmation or additional information. A payment confirmation does not prove seller dispatch.
When domestic tracking is added, note the carrier and latest scan. A domestic delivery marked complete means the seller’s parcel reached its recorded destination; it does not itself prove warehouse QC completion or that the correct variant was received. For a stock or dispatch question, use the purchase order ID rather than an international tracking number that does not exist yet.
Warehouse receiving, QC and your decision

Receiving can include parcel identification, item checking, photographs, weighing and recording. Compare the warehouse product record with your saved listing and variant. If the order shows delivery but no warehouse record, check whether the domestic tracking number was registered correctly, particularly for self-purchased forwarding items.
Once evidence appears, decide whether to accept, request clarification or pursue eligible after-sales. Keep uncertain or wrong goods out of the international parcel. The seller’s return window and warehouse storage allowance are separate; waiting for other purchases can use up the seller’s time limit.
Packing or rehearsal is not carrier transit

Selecting items and submitting a parcel starts a preparation stage. Instructions may require packing, reinforcement, removal of disposable packaging or measurement. A rehearsal result supplies information for a shipping decision; it does not mean the parcel has left the warehouse.
Read whether the account is waiting for your approval, an extra payment or a route selection. Check final weight, dimensions and total payable amount before confirming. If preparation exceeds the service’s displayed processing range, send the parcel number and submission timestamp to the platform’s support channel.
Label created and carrier accepted

A tracking number can be allocated before the carrier physically receives the box. “Label created” or equivalent electronic information is different from a pickup or acceptance scan. Cross-check the agent handoff record with the named carrier’s tracking page. Some routes also allocate a final-mile number later.
For example, an agent parcel number might identify your grouped warehouse items while a separate tracking number identifies the carrier’s shipment. Record both in your notes. Do not enter the purchase order ID into a carrier form and conclude that the shipment is missing when it returns no match.
International movement and delivery

Read scans in order, keeping their displayed time zones in mind. Export handling, transit and final-mile events may come from different logistics partners. A gap between scans is not enough by itself to identify loss. Compare with the current route’s expected processing range and the messages in your account.
When a delivery scan appears but the parcel is not found, check the delivery location information and the carrier’s available evidence. Contact the platform or carrier through its stated enquiry process, providing the shipment reference and the relevant scan. If packaging or contents are damaged, preserve the box and the evidence requested under the applicable claim terms.
Send a support request that can be investigated

Include the relevant order or parcel ID, carrier and tracking number, destination country, last scan with date, the stage that appears stalled and your specific question. Attach the account status and tracking screenshots while obscuring unnecessary personal or payment information. Keep messages in the official support channel.
An example: “Parcel [ID] was submitted on [date]. The account shows [status], and carrier tracking [number] last shows [event/date]. Please confirm whether the box has been handed to the carrier and whether another tracking number applies.” This is clearer than asking only why an order is slow.
Tracking questions answered

Does a label mean the parcel is moving? No; look for handoff or acceptance evidence. Does domestic delivery mean international delivery? No; it is an earlier stage. Is every unchanged status a lost parcel? No; investigate against the expected range and actual scans.
Keep a timeline: purchase submitted, seller dispatched, domestic delivered, warehouse received, QC approved, parcel submitted, packed, paid, handed over and delivered. That record shows which stage needs attention and which reference number support needs.
